No traffic incident was recorded near the route in the trip window (F13) and the only speed records are band 4 (30–39 km/h) on Tampines Expressway and Punggol Road (F11, F12), which is neither a DataMall incident on the optimal route nor a band 1/2 record, so the driver's congestion claim is not corroborated traffic evidence and cannot justify the detour under RD-4.

The rider's money claim fails on the fare records: this is a fixed-quote RydeX trip with no surge (F5), the billed distance of 9.9 km does not exceed the optimal route of 9.9 km (F4), and the $23.32 total is exactly base $3.90 + distance $14.02 + time $3.93 + platform $1.47 with waiting $0.00 (F6) — no unpublished add-on and no overcharge, so no refund is computable.

Even though the deviation is exempt by the rider's own consent, the record should note the driver's breach of RD-1 and support an account review: the driver has one upheld dispute in the last 90 days (F16), so this is a repeated pattern for Ryde to examine.

There is no safety element to escalate: the chat contains only the driver's routing request and the rider's agreement (F7, F8, F9, F10), with no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, and the weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain (F14).

weaknesses: The rider's own message at 10:01 (F8) is exactly the consent RD-5 requires, sent before the segment start recorded in F3, which extinguishes the only off-route segment in the case — this is the decisive fact against any route refund.

The complaint asserts the rider 'paid more than the estimate', but the system fare record contradicts it: billed distance 9.9 km equals the optimal 9.9 km (F4) and the $23.32 total reconciles item-by-item with no unpublished charge (F6); a fixed-quote fare is indifferent to the +1.8 km in F1, so F1 is a fact the other side will use to defeat the monetary claim.
The rider's profile shows 2 disputes in 90 days with 0 upheld (F15), which the other side may cite as a pattern of unfounded fee complaints.

F2 shows the trip took 17.8 min against a 15 min estimate, but no clause compensates for extra time on a fixed-quote RydeX trip, so that fact helps only the driver's general reasonableness narrative and cannot be converted into money.

claims.assertion: The single off-route segment (10:04–10:07, +1.73 km) is covered by valid rider consent: the driver asked first and the rider's own message agreed. F7 (10:01, driver: "Traffic ahead on Tampines Expressway is building up, ok if I go round via Halus Link?") precedes the segment start of 10:04 in F3, and F8 (10:01, rider: "Sure, go ahead.") names exactly that route change, so it is consent to this segment under RD-5's 'before' test.
The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped (F9), so there is no evidence gap; the agreement in F8 can be read and given effect rather than sent to manual review.

This is not a case of a driver rerouting and telling the rider afterwards: the request (F7), the agreement (F8) and the driver's statement (F10) are all at 10:01, before the off-route segment began at 10:04 (F3), so per RD-5 the segment is exempted and the outcome for it is no_action.

The rider has already been billed the fixed quoted distance, not the extra km: the billed distance of 9.9 km equals the optimal route of 9.9 km (F4), so no distance-based overcharge exists. On a RydeX fixed quote, distance changes do not change the fare (RD-2 non-metered branch) and any refund is limited to undisclosed add-ons or ERP/toll items actually incurred.

There is no chargeable add-on to refund: the total of $23.32 (F6) contains base $3.90, distance $14.02, time $3.93, waiting $0.00, platform $1.47 and no discount, and there is no toll/ERP or manual extra line; the rider's "paid more than the estimate" is a quote-to-final comparison, not an excess item (F6).

The driver's reason for the reroute was genuine congestion rather than an unexplained deviation: Tampines Expressway was at speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) and Punggol Road at band 4 during 09:49–10:21, covering the segment window, with fair weather (F11, F12, F14). This supports the reasonable-cause explanation the driver gave at the time (F7), although RD-4(b) treats speed bands as corroboration only and no incident was recorded (F13).

No account flag is warranted against the driver: the profile shows only 1 upheld dispute in 90 days and 0 upheld route disputes (F16), so RD-6's 'repeated route offender' precondition (upheld route dispute in the last 90 days plus this case) is not met even if a violation were recorded.

weaknesses: The GPS record itself establishes an off-route segment: F3 shows 1.94 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.22 km (+1.73 km) and F1 shows +1.8 km actual vs optimal. The rider's advocate will argue this is an unexempted deviation under RD-1, and RD-1 sets no minimum threshold, so the deviation cannot be dismissed as trivial.

The exemption depends entirely on the consent messages F7/F8 being read as covering this segment. If the judge reads "go round via Halus Link" narrowly, or finds the consent does not extend to the specific off-route track in F3, the segment falls back to RD-2 and the driver is left with a recorded RD-1 breach.

RD-4 gives the driver no supporting exemption: F13 records no traffic incident on the optimal route, and F11/F12 are only speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) on the optimal route, which RD-4(b) treats as corroboration only — not enough to exempt the segment on its own (and RD-4(b)'s single-record sufficiency is an open point, G3).
F2 (17.8 min actual vs 15 min estimated) and F14 (fair weather, no rain) will be used to argue time was lost on a deviation with no weather excuse.

notices.text:
Your case is closed with no refund.

What decided it: the app charged you the fixed RydeX quote, not a metered fare. Your route was 1.8 km longer than the shortest one, but on a fixed-quote trip the extra distance doesn't change what you pay. The fare you were charged matches the published items exactly, and the extra 2.7 minutes of travel time isn't something we compensate for.

What it means for you: nothing changes on your account, and nothing is owed either way. You can keep using RydeX at the quoted price.

Your case is closed with no action against you.

What it means for you: the route deviation is noted on the trip file as excused, no refund is owed to the rider, and no flag is placed on your account.
